# Post-Write Delta and Second Pass

The Awtsmoos lets green tests stand before a harsher mirror, where hidden generations and false fears are tried;
Awtsmoos.com keeps only evidence-born corrections, so no needless rewrite can masquerade as a deeper guide.

## Original plan remembered

The original plan required a reusable dynamic reference-post abstraction, native Ikar Tanach source resolution, Daily Chitas as a virtual grouping, normal post-reader manifestation, native comments/social behavior, arbitrary week/date navigation, mobile-first controls, honest Hebrew/English semantics, no Chabad redirect, full regression coverage, readback, integration with current upstream, deployment, and public verification.

## What the first implementation actually wrote

- Native post-range references and resolver over persisted Ikar chapter posts.
- Chumash book-name adapter and aliyah range parser.
- Dynamic `chitas-YYYY-MM-DD` synthetic posts loaded before persisted post lookup.
- Canonical Hebrew source sections from Ikar with source post/section provenance.
- Daily Chitas schedule with ordinary aliyos, festival deferral, Diaspora/Israel cycle-turn behavior.
- Internal Living Path card routes with no `chabad.org`, `externalHref`, or `virtualStudy`.
- Native reader masthead with week/date and Hebrew/English-interface controls.
- Chitas-only Sunday-through-Shabbos week panel instead of generic TODAY timeline buckets.
- Native comment identity through `post.heichel.id`; the actual comment-tree endpoint returns HTTP 200.
- Honest translation status: English interface only because current native Tanach source/translation subsystem does not materialize an English Tanach body.
- Tests proving live Devarim 31:20–31:30 resolves exactly eleven canonical Ikar pesukim.

## Readback discoveries

### Delta 1 — stale module-generation URLs

Several files changed after their first `native-chitas-001` publication-shaped import was written. Local Node tests read disk directly and cannot expose this browser module-graph mismatch. The stale edges are:

- `virtual-series.js` → provider/schedule/week-state v001.
- `coordinates.js` → dynamicPost v001.
- `postManifest.js` → masthead v001.
- `dynamicPost.js` → rangeParser v001.
- `rangeParser.js` → books v001.
- changed date-policy dependencies imported without the Chitas generation marker.

Second pass: normalize changed Chitas edges to `native-chitas-002`. Keep the stable reference-post engine at `native-reference-post-001`.

### Delta 2 — suspected reader navigation bug disproved

Readback of `functions/ui/nav.js` proves the current native reader already has Chitas-aware navigation. It resolves target post IDs from `series.posts`, produces canonical `/series/daily-chitas/post/chitas-YYYY-MM-DD` links, updates `chitasDate`, and localizes day navigation. No rewrite is justified.

### Delta 3 — global cache-bust churn disproved

Local JavaScript responses include `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, ETags, and Last-Modified. Reloaded module URLs revalidate. The global `heichel-mobile-007` entry does not require a speculative bump merely because Chitas descendants changed. Keep the global cache covenant stable and correct only explicit stale Chitas descendant generation markers.

### Delta 4 — synthetic comments verified

`/api/social/heichelos/ikar/posts/chitas-2026-09-05/comment-tree` returns HTTP 200 with the ordinary empty-thread structure. No special comments backend and no persisted duplicate Torah post are needed.

### Delta 5 — English Torah translation remains unavailable

The canonical Ikar Tanach chapter posts expose Hebrew pasuk sections. The existing native translation client intentionally supports Sichos/meluket-style series and returns early for Tanach book series. The interface must not claim translated Torah exists. Keep `translationStatus: canonical_hebrew_only` and label the control `English UI`.

## Second-pass files to rewrite completely

1. `heichel/modules/chitas/week-state.js` — version date-policy import.
2. `heichel/modules/chitas/hebcal-provider.js` — version date-policy import.
3. `heichel/modules/chitas/schedule.js` — version constants/date-policy imports.
4. `heichel/modules/chitas/virtual-series.js` — use v002 provider/schedule/week-state.
5. `post/logic/chitas/rangeParser.js` — use v002 books adapter.
6. `post/logic/chitas/dynamicPost.js` — use v002 range parser.
7. `post/logic/initialization/coordinates.js` — use v002 dynamic post.
8. `post/logic/initialization/postManifest.js` — use v002 masthead.
9. `tests/geelooy/chitasLivingPathContract.test.mjs` — add a static generation-coherence contract over browser-facing Chitas owners.

## What will not be rewritten

- `functions/ui/nav.js`: already correct and owned by a broader reader-navigation change.
- global Heichel script versions: revalidation evidence removes the need.
- Torah source posts/database: canonical source must remain singular.
- comments APIs: ordinary synthetic ID flow is already accepted.
- external study redirects: already removed and must remain absent.

## Verification after second pass

Run syntax, <=120-line contract, schedule tests, native-range live resolution, Living Path contract, UX contract, comment-tree HTTP witness, generation-coherence grep, `git diff --check`, then re-read every rewritten file. Write a fresh `06-...` final plan-vs-actual audit. If that audit discovers any source delta, perform another complete-file pass before integration.

The Awtsmoos does not ask a passing test to carry what only readback can reveal;
Awtsmoos.com lets evidence prune false branches, until one coherent browser generation remains real.
